## Veredicto sobre A/B/C (con dato nuevo de la hoja de datos)

Coincido contigo en **A**, y acabo de confirmar un hecho del datasheet oficial de Renesas que la **refuerza** y al mismo tiempo **acota el puzzle**:

> "The ISL29125 is designed to **reject IR** in light sources" — tiene filtro bloqueador de IR físico.

Esto implica una corrección importante respecto a lo que dice `docs/spike-a-axis-blade-detection.md`:

- El **ISL29125 (0x44) NO ve IR**. Es el sensor de **color → es el detector de MARCAS** (lee el papel bajo luz visible). Por eso Cricut exige "calibrar en zona iluminada" — exactamente lo que dice tu hipótesis A.
- El **emisor IR (knob superior, siempre encendido) NO alimenta al ISL29125**. Alimenta a un **receptor IR separado = detector de hoja**, que es lo que aún no hemos localizado.

Con eso:
- **B (IR vía EEPROM I2C)**: descartada — el escaneo I2C completo solo dio 0x44 (sin EEPROM 0x50 ni segundo respondedor).
- **C (IR trucado con encoder)**: descartada — el bench `S` mostró que las líneas encoder son cuadratura pura.
- **A**: correcta en lo esencial: *dos* funciones ópticas (marca=color+IR-rechazado, hoja=IR), compartiendo bus/recursos. Lo que queda abierto es **dónde reporta el receptor IR de hoja**.

## Hallazgos concretos del probeo en vivo (esta sesión)

- Mapa de registros **confirmado** ISL29125 (32 regs, alias módulo 32 — 0x20-0x3F == 0x00-0x1F, así que **no hay registros altos ocultos**, hipótesis "0x40+" muerta).
- **Corrección al doc**: el ID `0x7D` está en **reg 0x1E (30), no en 0x00**. Reg 0x00 lee `3`. El `selftest` de `sensors_isl.c:247` lee 0x00 y por tanto **falla en máquina** (comprueba el registro equivocado). No bloquea la detección, pero hay que corregirlo.
- Estado óptico actual (hoja puesta, tool arriba): **GREEN=1793, RED=769, BLUE=769**. GREEN domina → luz visible llegando por el tubo de luz (no IR).

## La pregunta que decide A de una vez

**¿El ISL29125 recibe la luz del emisor IR?** El datasheet dice que no (filtro IR). Un único test físico lo cierra:

**Test de oclusión del emisor (sin reflash, sin movimiento):** tapa SOLO el knob superior (emisor, el que brilla rosa en la cámara) con un dedo o cinta opaca, mientras yo leo `c` en vivo. 
- Si GREEN/RED/BLUE **no cambian** → el ISL29125 no ve el emisor → **A confirmada** (el receptor de hoja es otro, separado del color).
- Si **cambian** → el sensor sí ve IR → la variante Cricut no rechaza IR → matiz a A.

Luego, para localizar el receptor IR de hoja, lo más rentable es añadir al spike un **escaneo I2C completo (0x03-0x77) + toggle de GPIOs candidatos (mux select) con re-escaneo** — eso ataca directamente el "plexa" de A. Implica reflash (PAUSE+encendido).

¿Hacemos primero el test del emisor (tú tapas, yo leo)? Y en paralelo te preparo el firmware de escaneo I2C + mux.

Let me look at isl_read_reg again:
```c
static uint8_t isl_read_reg(uint8_t reg, uint8_t *val) {
    ...
    i2c_start();
    i2c_write_byte(ISL_ADDR << 1);   // write addr
    if (i2c_read_ack()) {
        i2c_write_byte(reg);          // write register
        if (i2c_read_ack()) {
            i2c_start();              // repeated start
            i2c_write_byte((ISL_ADDR << 1) | 1);  // read addr
            if (i2c_read_ack()) {
                *val = i2c_read_byte();  // read ONE byte
                i2c_write_ack();         // NACK (end)
                i2c_stop();
                return 1;
            }
        }
    }
    ...
}
```

This reads ONE byte per register. For a 16-bit register (like GREEN), this reads the FIRST byte (GREEN_L) and the register auto-increments to GREEN_H, but we NACK and stop, so we only get GREEN_L.

```c
typedef enum {
```

Flow:
- `m` command: reset mux_idx=0, mux_sub=0, mux_addr=0, clear mux_base, state=SPIKE_MUX_RUN.
- mux_tick() per call:
  - if mux_sub == 0 (baseline): probe addr, record in mux_base, advance addr; when addr > 0x77, print baseline responders, move to mux_sub=1 (set pin HIGH).
  - if mux_sub == 1 (HIGH scan): probe addr, if ACK != mux_base[addr], print "[M] pin HIGH diff addr=X (base=%d now=%d)". advance; when done, move mux_sub=2 (set pin LOW).
  - if mux_sub == 2 (LOW scan): probe addr, diff vs base. advance; when done, move to next pin (mux_idx++, mux_sub=1 or done).

```c
        /* baseline scan */
        if (mux_addr <= 0x77) {
            mux_base[mux_addr] = sensors_isl_probe(mux_addr) ? 1 : 0;
            mux_addr++;
            return;
        }
        /* done baseline */
        printString("[M] baseline:");
        for (a = 0x03; a <= 0x77; a++) if (mux_base[a]) { printString(" "); printInteger(a); }
        printString("\r\n");
        mux_phase = 1;
        mux_pin = 0;
        mux_addr = 0x03;
        GPIO_PinOutputEnable(mux_pins[mux_pin].p);
        GPIO_PinWrite(mux_pins[mux_pin].p, true);
        printString("[M] "); printString(mux_pins[mux_pin].n); printString(" HIGH ...\r\n");
        return;
    }

    if (mux_phase == 1 || mux_phase == 2) {
        if (mux_addr <= 0x77) {
            ack = sensors_isl_probe(mux_addr) ? 1 : 0;
            if (ack != mux_base[mux_addr]) {
                printString("[M] ");
                printString(mux_pins[mux_pin].n);
                printString(mux_phase == 1 ? " HIGH " : " LOW  ");
                printString("diff addr=");
                printInteger(mux_addr);
                printString(" base=");
                printInteger(mux_base[mux_addr]);
                printString(" now=");
                printInteger(ack);
                printString("\r\n");
            }
            mux_addr++;
            return;
        }
        /* done this phase */
        if (mux_phase == 1) {
            mux_phase = 2;
            mux_addr = 0x03;
            GPIO_PinWrite(mux_pins[mux_pin].p, false);
            return;
        } else {
            /* done LOW; next pin */
            GPIO_PinInputEnable(mux_pins[mux_pin].p); /* restore to input (safe) */
            mux_pin++;
            if (mux_pin >= sizeof(mux_pins)/sizeof(mux_pins[0])) {
                printString("[M] mux hunt done\r\n");
                spike_state = SPIKE_STREAM;
                spike_next_ms = timer_get_ms();
                return;
            }
            mux_phase = 1;
            mux_addr = 0x03;
            GPIO_PinOutputEnable(mux_pins[mux_pin].p);
            GPIO_PinWrite(mux_pins[mux_pin].p, true);
            return;
        }
    }
}
```

The PIC32MX 10-bit ADC standard configuration:
- AD1CON1: 
  - bit 15 ON = 1 (enable)
  - bit 13 ADSIDL = 0
  - bits 10-8 FORM = 0 (unsigned integer)
  - bits 7-5 SSRC = 0b111 (internal counter / auto-convert) OR 0b000 (clearing SAMP)
  - bit 2 ASAM = 1 (auto-sample)
  - bit 1 SAMP = 0
  - bit 0 DONE = read-only
- AD1CON2:
  - VCFG<2:0> = 0 (AVDD/AVSS reference)
  - OFFCAL, etc. = 0
  - SMPI = 0 (interrupt after 1 sample)
  - BUFM = 0
  - ALTS = 0
- AD1CON3:
  - ADRC = 0 (use system clock, TAD = TCY)
  - ADCS<7:0> = TAD divisor
  - SAMC<4:0> = auto-sample time
- AD1CHS:
  - CH0SA<4:0> = channel 0 positive input (AN0-AN27)
  - CH0NA = 0 (VREF-)
- AD1CSSL: channel scan (0 = manual)

1. Select channel in AD1CHS.CH0SA.

## Assistant (build · mimo-v2.5-free · 13.9s)

_Thinking:_

All tasks completed. Let me summarize the findings for the user.

**Summary of what we accomplished:**

1. **Root cause found**: ISL29125 requires reading reg 0x09 (GREEN low byte) before 0x0A (GREEN high byte). Without the priming read, 0x0A returns stale data (0–3 instead of the real value).

import glob, serial, time, re

dev = sorted(glob.glob('/dev/ttyACM*'))[0]
s = serial.Serial(dev, 115200, timeout=0.1)
s.reset_input_buffer()
time.sleep(2.5)

def jog(cmd, wait):
    s.reset_input_buffer()
    s.write(cmd.encode()+b'\r\n'); s.flush()
    time.sleep(wait)
    d = s.read(65536).decode('ascii','replace')
    steps = None
    for l in d.split('\n'):
        if 'done' in l:
            m = re.search(r'steps=(\d+)', l)
            if m: steps = int(m.group(1))
    return steps

def refl():
    s.reset_input_buffer()
    time.sleep(0.8)
    d = s.read(65536).decode('ascii','replace')
    tel = [l.strip() for l in d.split('\n') if l.strip().startswith('[T]')]
    m = re.search(r'z2=(\d+) a=(-?\d+) refl=(\d+) blade=(\d+)', tel[-1]) if tel else None
    return m.groups() if m else None

# Raise to top (stall)
st = jog('z2 cw 5000 2200', 6.0)
print(f'TOP: jog_steps={st}, tel={refl()}')

# Lower in 1000-step cycles, profile refl
for i in range(12):
    st = jog('z2 ccw 400 2200', 1.8)
    t = refl()
    print(f'DOWN {i+1}: dz={st} tel={t}')
    if t and int(t[2]) < 10 and i > 3:  # refl collapsed -> left the window
        print('  (refl collapsed, stopping descent)')
        break

# Back to top
st = jog('z2 cw 5000 2200', 6.0)
print(f'BACK TO TOP: jog_steps={st}, tel={refl()}')

s.close()
" 2>&1

import glob, serial, time, re

dev = sorted(glob.glob('/dev/ttyACM*'))[0]
s = serial.Serial(dev, 115200, timeout=0.1)
s.reset_input_buffer()
time.sleep(2.5)

def jog(cmd, wait):
    s.reset_input_buffer()
    s.write(cmd.encode()+b'\r\n'); s.flush()
    time.sleep(wait)
    d = s.read(65536).decode('ascii','replace')
    st = None
    for l in d.split('\n'):
        if 'done' in l:
            m = re.search(r'steps=(\d+)', l)
            if m: st = int(m.group(1))
    return st

def refl():
    s.reset_input_buffer()
    time.sleep(0.8)
    d = s.read(65536).decode('ascii','replace')
    tel = [l.strip() for l in d.split('\n') if l.strip().startswith('[T]')]
    m = re.search(r'a=(-?\d+) refl=(\d+) blade=(\d+)', tel[-1]) if tel else None
    return m.groups() if m else None

# Descend ~1200 steps from top (small jogs for control)
total = 0
for i in range(3):
    st = jog('z2 ccw 300 2200', 1.6)
    total += st or 0
    print(f'down jog {i+1}: dz={st} (total {total})')

print('refl at height:', refl())

# Arm + capture A rotation at this height
s.write(b'arm\r\n'); s.flush(); time.sleep(2); s.read(65536)
s.write(b'cap 12000 2200\r\n'); s.flush(); time.sleep(17)
data = s.read(65536).decode('ascii','replace')
s.close()
with open('/tmp/cap_a_low.csv','w') as f: f.write(data)
samples = re.findall(r'^(-?\d+),(\d+)', data, re.M)
if samples:
    a_vals = [int(a) for a,r in samples]
    r_vals = [int(r) for a,r in samples]
    print(f'samples={len(samples)} a_delta={a_vals[-1]-a_vals[0]} refl: min={min(r_vals)} max={max(r_vals)}')
    # refl histogram
    from collections import Counter
    print('refl histogram:', dict(Counter(r_vals).most_common(8)))
" 2>&1

**Tool: bash** rm -f /tmp/cutcutgo-tty-*.lock; python3 -c "
import glob, serial, time, re

dev = sorted(glob.glob('/dev/ttyACM*'))[0]
s = serial.Serial(dev, 115200, timeout=0.1)
s.reset_input_buffer()
time.sleep(2.5)

def tel():
    s.reset_input_buffer()
    time.sleep(0.7)
    d = s.read(65536).decode('ascii','replace')
    tl = [l.strip() for l in d.split('\n') if l.strip().startswith('[T]')]
    if not tl: return None
    m = re.search(r'a=(-?\d+) refl=(\d+) blade=(\d+)', tl[-1])
    return (int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))) if m else None

def jog_verified(cmd, wait, expect_axis, stall_max=150):
    'send jog, verify response, return True if stalled (delta small)'
    for _ in range(3):
        before = tel()
        b = before[0] if expect_axis=='a' else None
        s.reset_input_buffer()
        s.write(cmd.encode()+b'\r\n'); s.flush()
        time.sleep(wait)
        d = s.read(65536).decode('ascii','replace')
        done = 'done' in d
        after = tel()
        if not done or after is None: continue
        return True, before, after
    return False, None, None

# Ensure armed
s.write(b'arm\r\n'); s.flush(); time.sleep(2); s.read(65536)

results = []
for cycle in range(16):
    # 0. Verify at top (short jog, must stall)
    ok, b, a = jog_verified('z2 cw 600 2200', 1.6, 'z')
    if not ok or (a[0]-b[0] if b else 999) > 150:
        # not stalled: raise longer
        jog_verified('z2 cw 5000 2200', 6.0, 'z')
    # 1. Rotate A (450ms at 2000)
    ok, b, a = jog_verified('a cw 450 2000', 1.8, 'a')
    if not ok: print(f'cycle {cycle}: A jog LOST'); continue
    ang = (b[0], a[0])
    # 2. Plunge to stall
    ok, b2, a2 = jog_verified('z2 ccw 5500 2200', 6.5, 'z')
    # verify bottom stall with short jog
    ok3, b3, a3 = jog_verified('z2 ccw 600 2200', 1.6, 'z')
    stalled = ok3 and a3 and b3 and (a3[0]-b3[0]) <= 150
    if not stalled:
        jog_verified('z2 ccw 3000 2200', 4.0, 'z')
    refl_bot = a3[1] if a3 else -1
    # 3. Raise to top
    jog_verified('z2 cw 5500 2200', 6.5, 'z')
    ok4, b4, a4 = jog_verified('z2 cw 600 2200', 1.6, 'z')
    top_ok = ok4 and a4 and b4 and (a4[0]-b4[0]) <= 150
    if not top_ok:
        jog_verified('z2 cw 3000 2200', 4.0, 'z')
    refl_top = a4[1] if a4 else -1
    results.append((ang, refl_bot, refl_top))
    print(f'cycle {cycle+1:2d}: a {ang[0]}->{ang[1]} (d={ang[1]-ang[0]:+6d})  refl_bot={refl_bot:3d} refl_top={refl_top:3d}')

print()
print('=== refl_bot vs angle profile ===')
for ang, rb, rt in results:
    print(f'a_end={ang[1]:>7} refl_bot={rb:3d} refl_top={rt}')
s.close()
" 2>&1

import glob, serial, time, re

dev = sorted(glob.glob('/dev/ttyACM*'))[0]
s = serial.Serial(dev, 115200, timeout=0.1)
s.reset_input_buffer()
time.sleep(2.5)

def tel():
    s.reset_input_buffer()
    time.sleep(0.6)
    d = s.read(65536).decode('ascii','replace')
    tl = [l.strip() for l in d.split('\n') if l.strip().startswith('[T]')]
    if not tl: return None
    m = re.search(r'z2=(\d+).*refl=(\d+) blade=(\d+)', tl[-1])
    return (int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))) if m else None

def jog(cmd, wait):
    s.reset_input_buffer()
    s.write(cmd.encode()+b'\r\n'); s.flush()
    time.sleep(wait)
    d = s.read(65536).decode('ascii','replace')
    return 'done' in d

# Raise to top stall
for i in range(3):
    b = tel()
    jog('z2 cw 5000 2200', 5.5)
    b2 = tel()
    jog('z2 cw 600 2200', 1.5)
    a = tel()
    dz = (a[0]-b2[0]) if (b2 and a) else 999
    print(f'raise {i+1}: stall_dz={dz} refl={a[1] if a else \"?\"} blade={a[2] if a else \"?\"}')
    if dz <= 150:
        print('TOP REACHED')
        break

s.close()
" 2>&1

**Tool: bash** rm -f /tmp/cutcutgo-tty-*.lock; timeout 130 python3 -u -c "
import glob, serial, time, re

dev = sorted(glob.glob('/dev/ttyACM*'))[0]
s = serial.Serial(dev, 115200, timeout=0.1)
s.reset_input_buffer()
time.sleep(2.5)

def tel():
    s.reset_input_buffer()
    time.sleep(0.55)
    d = s.read(65536).decode('ascii','replace')
    tl = [l.strip() for l in d.split('\n') if l.strip().startswith('[T]')]
    if not tl: return None
    m = re.search(r'a=(-?\d+) refl=(\d+)', tl[-1])
    return (int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))) if m else None

def jog(cmd, wait):
    s.reset_input_buffer()
    s.write(cmd.encode()+b'\r\n'); s.flush()
    time.sleep(wait)
    d = s.read(65536).decode('ascii','replace')
    return 'done' in d

s.write(b'arm\r\n'); s.flush(); time.sleep(2); s.read(65536)

pts = []
prev = tel()
for i in range(24):
    jog('a cw 150 2000', 1.3)
    time.sleep(0.9)
    cur = tel()
    if not cur or prev is None: continue
    pts.append((cur[0], cur[1]))
    print(f'a={cur[0]:>7} d={cur[0]-prev[0]:+5d} refl={cur[1]:>3} ' + '#'*cur[1])
    prev = cur
    with open('/tmp/fine_rev.csv','a') as f:
        f.write(f'{cur[0]},{cur[1]}\n')

refs = [p[1] for p in pts]
print(f'\\nrefl: min={min(refs)} max={max(refs)} span={max(refs)-min(refs)} samples={len(pts)}')
s.close()
" 2>&1

So the bottleneck is the I2C read itself (mark_detector_read does priming + real read, each isl_read_reg = ~10-15 bytes bit-banged at maybe slow GPIO speed... 36ms/sample total). Fine.

2. **PWM/speed semantics confirmed**: OCxRS higher = slower (A4950 slow-decay wiring, duty inverted). OCxR never written (0) — hal_motor_set_speed writes OCxRS only. My attempted OCxR fix was wrong and reverted.

3. **Z2 axis mechanics**: spur gear + return spring (user confirmed). Top stall = frame stop. Bottom stall = collar vs sensor-piece stop = **the tool-check endstop**. Full travel ≈ 6900-7000 encoder steps. Jog speed 2200 = ~2.2-3.2 steps/ms free; stall detect = jog and verify dz ≤ 150 (repeat short jog after long jog: dz≈0 = stalled).

4. **A axis mechanics**: worm gear (self-locking, cannot hand-rotate — normal!). ~17000-17500 encoder steps per blade revolution.

5. **A4950 thermal latch**: sustained PWM (>1-2s) on stalled/near-stalled A → driver latches OFF until power cycle. Short pulses (150-600ms) with cooldowns always work. Symptom: a-delta freezes mid-cap; recovered only by USB power cycle.

6. **Safety confirmed the hard way**: rotating A with blade semi-down (~2900 steps from top) → motor crawls/stalls (blade rubbing collar). NEVER rotate unless at top stall.
